links.targetTitle: USDC-to-DAI swaps are all-or-nothing and loop the PSM's own

title: The DAI-USDS migrator is the one Liquidity Layer swap with neither a rate limit nor a slippage check, because the exchange is 1:1 by construction
content:
A.6.1.1.2.2.6.1.2.2.1.2.1.2.12.1 and A...12.2 are the shortest procedures in the module: check `onlyRole(RELAYER)`, approve the `daiUsds` migrator, call `usdsToDai` or `daiToUsds`. No `_rateLimited`, no minimum output, no balance-delta verification, no configured slippage.

The justification is stated in the steps themselves — `daiUsds` "facilitates a **1:1** swap between USDS and DAI" (A...12.1.2) and the swap is executed "in a 1:1 ratio" (A...12.1.3). A fixed-parity conversion has no execution price, so slippage protection has nothing to protect against, and it moves value between two representations of the same unit, so a rate limit would meter an action that changes no exposure.

This clarifies what Grove's controls are actually for. Rate limits are not a generic activity throttle — they bound **exposure to a counterparty or market**. Where an operation creates none, applying one would only add a failure mode and a governance parameter to maintain.

The assumption doing the load-bearing work is that parity is structural rather than market-determined. It is inherited from the migrator contract, so if that contract ever became fee-bearing or path-dependent, these two functions would be the ones with no defence — and, like the other unguarded paths in this chunk, their only remaining control would be the relayer role.
description: swapUSDSToDAI and swapDAIToUSDS carry only the RELAYER gate; a fixed-parity conversion between two Sky-issued units changes no economic exposure, so there is nothing to meter.
